headline_stat.name: CA1 units significantly theta phase-locked (Rayleigh p<0.05, running)

justification.dataset: DANDI 000044 dorsal CA1 (Grosmark & Buzsáki) is a canonical, expert-standard choice for theta phase entrainment.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile with correct CA1-unit selection and spike-phase interpolation, but the speed computation classifies ~98% of the maze session as running, so the movement filter is essentially inert.
justification.analysis: Bandpass-Hilbert phase with MRL and a correctly implemented Rayleigh test is the right method, but no shuffle/circular-shift control is included and the Rayleigh test is anticonservative on autocorrelated within-cycle spikes.
justification.correctness: Reported counts, MRLs, phases, and spike totals reproduce exactly from the committed CSV and are internally consistent with all figures; MRLs are valid effect sizes that make the conclusion robust independent of the marginal p-values.
justification.figures: Figures clearly show the effect with labeled units and sample sizes, example units ranked by MRL (the effect metric), and a convincing pooled phase histogram and population summary.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to a genuinely strong result with nothing misrepresented, but no specific limitation (single session, single-channel reference, anticonservative test, low-n MRL inflation) is named.
